parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime is dominated by a national layer that is traveller-facing by design: passports must now show sex assigned at birth, X-markers are frozen, and a consular cable directs officers to refuse cases where documents 'cast doubt' on sex and to weigh lifetime fraud findings for visitors — a universal-exposure measure every crossing carries. Documented follow-on harms (strandings, birth-sex custody placement, corrections policies described as forced de-transition, sexual abuse in immigration custody) and a bathroom-trespass arrest in one state/province sit at tiers 1–2 of the precedence ladder. This state/province adds a minors' care ban and school facility restriction but no adult facility law, and some partial recourse exists (national hate-crime statute, employment rulings, municipal ordinances, courts enjoining several orders). Severity is high but not at the 0.05 tier: no execution pathway, contested litigation partially blunts enforcement. High Risk band.

entry_documents.exposure: Documented: passports must show sex assigned at birth; X-markers frozen; consular cable instructs officers to refuse cases with document doubt and consider permanent fraud ineligibility; travellers report confiscation/strandings.
entry_documents.protection: Ongoing litigation against the passport policy; fraud finding requires all four elements and is never automatic.
entry_documents.interaction: Border screening is the first operative stage for every visitor; document discrepancy can escalate into investigation and fraud referral.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented: national corrections bureau mandates hair-cutting, hormone removal and 'psychiatric' substitution for trans inmates; immigration custody shows forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans men; bathroom-law arrest led to 24h men's-ward custody.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented as operative for visitors; earlier prison LGBTQ order rescinded.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any arrest, immigration hold or hospital admission routes visitors into birth-sex custody systems.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Documented: 19+ state/provinces ban congruent facilities in government buildings; 4 criminalise in some circumstances; here, only the K-12 school restriction binds — no adult facility restriction documented in this state/province.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State/province guidance tells districts to 'proceed cautiously'; no adult-wide ban locally.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National facilities ban reaches federal buildings everywhere; state-level patchwork governs the rest.

care_services.exposure: Documented: minors' care ban in force here with no phase-out; national proposals to bar insurance for under-18 care; hospitals subpoenaed for under-19 records.
care_services.protection: Adult care access not documented as restricted locally; conversion therapy barred for minors since Sept 2024.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor needing refills or care hits the ban directly; the accompanying adult faces investigation risk via hospital records.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented: state framing of trans identity as fraud/misrepresentation at consular level; counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups; police arrested capitol protesters and a bathroom user.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing conditions local police discretion; hate-crime statute here excludes gender identity.

minors_guardians.exposure: Documented: care ban for minors with no continuity provision; school sports and bathroom restrictions; criminal prosecution threatened for teachers facilitating social transition.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian of a trans minor faces care denial, record exposure and potential criminalisation of facilitation.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Not documented at trans-specific rate for this state/province; hate-crime enhancement excludes gender identity locally.
street_violence_police_response.protection: 19 municipal non-discrimination ordinances; national employment rulings; sexual-orientation hate-crime cases prosecuted.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Victims of bias violence here lack the state enhancement, relying on general law.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Uncertain: unresolved scope of religious-freedom refusals, appellate status of care ban, and national employment protection; recourse is patchwork and litigation-dependent.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National hate-crime statute, municipal ordinances, enjoined orders, and legal-aid passport FAQ operate.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Court injunctions partially blunt national measures but exposure depends on timing of travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: Exceeds 0.35-A in severity: that anchor's harms are exclusion and humiliation, while the parent regime documents custody abuse, de-transition mandates and fraud-lifetime-ban framing aimed at visitors, though enforcement of worst outcomes is contested.

Below 0.15-C: no street sweeps or morality units targeting visitors, no credible execution pathway, courts actively enjoining measures, and recognised marriage plus partial protective machinery — the state is a bystander-protector in places, not a systematic persecutor of travellers.

Below 0.55-C in outcome severity: that anchor's worst case is ward misplacement and care delay; here the documented worst case includes men's-ward detention of a bathroom user, birth-sex custody, and detention sexual abuse — materially harsher consequences after discovery.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime travellers meet is a national exposure layer (entry documents, fraud framing, custody, care records) interacting with a state layer that is comparatively less restrictive for adults — no adult facility ban, partial municipal and judicial protections — but harsh for minors (care ban, school restrictions, prosecution threats for facilitation). Universal-exposure document screening at entry plus documented custodial harms place this above the administrative-exclusion tier but below jurisdictions with organised street-level targeting or lethal pathways. Litigation, injunctions, hate-crime statutes and municipal ordinances supply genuine but incomplete recourse, keeping the case in the High Risk band rather than Severe Risk.
